summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2 and node3 (standbys) on CentOS Stream 10, secured with a dedicated cluster CA. All replication traffic uses TLS (sslmode=verify-full) and pg_hba.conf on node1 restricts replication connections to hostssl with clientcert=verify-full for the 'replicator' role, so only peers with a certificate signed by the cluster CA can replicate. Verified negative cases (no cert, and a non-CA self-signed cert) are rejected. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes, proving boot-id change and full data/replication recovery after each restart, including a live write propagating to both standbys post-restart.
actions_performed: Installed postgresql-server 16.14 on node1, node2, node3 via dnf
Generated a cluster CA (ca.key/ca.crt) on node1 and issued server certs for node1/node2/node3 (with SAN DNS+IP) and a client cert for role 'replicator', all signed by that CA
Distributed certs to node2/node3 over SSH using the cluster keypair

Initialized primary data dir on node1 (postgresql-setup --initdb), installed server.crt/server.key/root.crt, configured postgresql.conf (listen_addresses, ssl on, wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders, hot_standby) and pg_hba.conf (hostssl replication replicator ... cert clientcert=verify-full)
Created replicator role with REPLICATION LOGIN on node1, started/enabled postgresql
Opened firewalld port 5432/tcp on all three nodes
Ran pg_basebackup with -R and TLS client-cert conninfo from node2 and node3 against node1, producing standby.signal and primary_conninfo with sslmode=verify-full and client cert paths
Added TLS server settings to node2/node3 postgresql.conf and started/enabled postgresql on both as standbys
Verified pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both standbys streaming with ssl=t and correct client cert serial
Verified data written on primary appears on both standbys (pg_is_in_recovery=t)

Negative-tested: connection without any client cert is rejected ('connection requires a valid client certificate'); connection with a freshly generated self-signed (non-CA) cert is rejected at TLS handshake ('unknown ca')
Relocated CA private key/cert from /tmp to /etc/pki/postgresql-ca with 700/600 permissions and cleaned up temp cert files
Captured baseline boot_id and health (postgresql active, replication streaming/recovering, repl_test row count) on all three nodes
Restarted node2, then node3, then node1 (primary last) one at a time via 'systemctl reboot' launched detached so the ack returned before disconnection; polled each until exec was available again

Confirmed changed boot_id on each node after its restart, confirmed postgresql active and standbys back in recovery/streaming with data intact after each restart, and confirmed node1 primary healthy with both standbys reconnected via TLS after its own restart
Performed a final post-restart write on node1 and confirmed it replicated to node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: PostgreSQL streaming replication configured with node1 as writable primary, node2/node3 as standbys
evidence.summary: node1 initialized as primary with wal_level=replica and replicator role; node2/node3 base-backed up with -R generating standby.signal; pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both streaming; both standbys show pg_is_in_recovery=t and see the row inserted on node1

evidence.requirement: Replication traffic carried over TLS using a cluster-created CA
evidence.summary: CA generated (ca.key/ca.crt) and used to sign node1/node2/node3 server certs and the replicator client cert; primary's postgresql.conf enables ssl with those certs; pg_basebackup succeeded using sslmode=verify-full with the CA-signed client cert; pg_stat_replication join to pg_stat_ssl shows ssl=t for both standby connections

evidence.requirement: Replication connections accepted only from peers presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA
evidence.summary: pg_hba.conf restricts replication to hostssl ... cert clientcert=verify-full; a connection attempt with no client cert is rejected ('connection requires a valid client certificate'); a connection using a freshly generated self-signed (non-CA) certificate is rejected at the TLS layer ('unknown ca')

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: node2 baseline, restart, changed boot id, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id bf8b9d80... and healthy standby state captured; systemctl reboot issued; post-restart boot_id 593c91bc... (changed); postgresql active and pg_is_in_recovery=t with data intact; primary confirms node2 reconnected and streaming

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: node3 baseline, restart, changed boot id, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 71f12f87... and healthy standby state captured; systemctl reboot issued; post-restart boot_id dc4b0dd5... (changed); postgresql active and pg_is_in_recovery=t with data intact; primary confirms node3 reconnected and streaming

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: node1 (primary) baseline, restart, changed boot id, recovery, and full cluster health after last restart
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d4784d1b... and healthy primary/replication state captured; systemctl reboot issued; post-restart boot_id f2470216... (changed); postgresql active with ssl=on, data intact, and both standbys reconnected/streaming; a post-restart insert on node1 verified present on both node2 and node3, proving full recovery
